_about: Plain words (rule 6), a discipline check at the end of every reply to the person. Each fault becomes a debt: it is put in front of Claude at their next message, and a next reply that still carries it is refused work until a reply clears it. Change a number or a word here and save; the check reads this file at every call. This file is the home of the inside words.

length._about: A reply is at most maxWords words, unless their own message asks for a long one (one of longAskWords). Progress bars, the Saved: and Used: lines and web addresses are not counted.

sentences._about: Whole sentences, no label-and-fragment lines. A label line starts with a few words and a colon ("**Status:** merged"), or is a heading or a bold line alone. A fragment line is a list line of fewer than fragmentWords words that does not end like a sentence. A table is always counted. The reply is at fault when it has more than maxLabelLines such lines. A sitrep (they asked for one, or the reply has a "Needs you:" line) is shaped by its own check and is not read here. exemptLabels are never counted.

ease._about: Reading ease, by the Flesch score (the same count as the manuals' checker: 206.835 - 1.015 x words per sentence - 84.6 x syllables per word; 60 and above is plain English). A reply of at least minWords words of prose must reach minScore. Lower on purpose than the manuals' 60: a reply names their projects and tools, which costs syllables.

code._about: No file names, paths or code in a reply unless their own message asks for them (one of techAskWords).

insideWords._about: No inside word without its meaning. A word of the list in a reply is a fault unless they used it in their own message, the reply says what it means right after it (one of explainMarks follows the word), or the plain words given for it appear in the reply. Skill names with a hyphen (hive-scout, playwright-cli) and work codes (E5, W14, C6) count as inside words too. To add a word: one pair "the word": "the plain words to say instead". maxNamed: how many are named in the note.
